schema_grounding_notes: THREE disjoint PPI tables — each is independent, never join two of them together; pick ONE based on what the user asked:
ppi_association_string  → general functional interaction partners (all evidence); columns: association_gene_symbol, association_partner_gene_symbol, association_score
ppi_physical_string     → physical binding / complex subset only; columns: physical_gene_symbol, physical_partner_gene_symbol, physical_score

ppi_detailed_channels_string → per-channel evidence breakdown; columns: channel_gene_symbol, channel_partner_gene_symbol, neighborhood/fusion/cooccurence/coexpression/experimental/database/textmining, channel_combined_score

ALL per-channel scores (experimental, neighborhood, fusion, cooccurence, coexpression, database, textmining) are INTEGER SCORES 0–1000, never boolean. When the user asks 'with experimental evidence' or 'by experimental score', set experimental='requested' (SELECT it as output) — do NOT set it to 'True' or any boolean filter value
association_score / physical_score / channel_combined_score are integers 700–999 in this snapshot (pre-filtered to high-confidence edges ≥ 700); 900+ is highest confidence

ppi_association_string is bidirectional: every undirected edge appears in both directions, so a single filter on association_gene_symbol returns ALL of that gene's interaction partners in association_partner_gene_symbol — do NOT also match association_partner_gene_symbol
ppi_physical_string is the subset of ppi_association_string based solely on physical/binding evidence; same physical_gene_symbol/physical_partner_gene_symbol layout
protein_alias_string maps STRING protein IDs to external aliases (Ensembl, UniProt, RefSeq); query through protein_master_table_string.gene_symbol first
cooccurence is spelled without the double 'r' on disk — use this spelling verbatim in filters

co_output_rules.reason: per-channel scores are not interpretable without the overall combined score for context
raw alias strings are not interpretable without the canonical gene symbol

db_llm_rules:
COMPLEX / PATHWAY DECOMPOSITION — when the question names a complex or pathway rather than a single gene, expand to its member gene symbols in the WHERE clause:
  mTORC1 / TORC1           → gene_symbol IN [MTOR, RPTOR, MLST8, DEPTOR, AKT1S1]
  Polycomb / PRC2 / PcG    → gene_symbol IN [EZH2, EED, SUZ12, RBBP4, JARID2]
  COP9 signalosome / CSN   → gene_symbol IN [COPS5, COPS8, COPS1, COPS2, COPS3, COPS4]
  cohesin complex          → gene_symbol IN [SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, STAG1, STAG2]
  nuclear pore basket      → gene_symbol IN [NUP153, NUP50, TPR, NUP98]
  ERK scaffold proteins    → gene_symbol IN [KSR1, KSR2, IQGAP1, SHOC2]
  Notch activation complex → gene_symbol IN [NOTCH1, RBPJ, MAML1, MAML2, EP300]
  Fanconi anemia complex   → gene_symbol IN [FANCD2, FANCA, BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2]
  mTORC2                   → gene_symbol IN [MTOR, RICTOR, MLST8, MAPKAP1, PRR5]
ANNOTATION ROUTING — for questions about function, role, disease involvement, modification, or 'is X involved in Y' (NOT 'who interacts with X'), use protein_master_table annotation column ONLY. Never PPI tables for these.
YES/NO PPI + NON-PPI PROPERTY — when asked 'Does X interact with Y [and also has property Z STRING does not store, e.g. circadian, temporal]': return the PPI edge (confirm interaction + score), then state STRING cannot confirm the additional property. NEVER return zero rows when the PPI component is answerable.
SLASH-SEPARATED NAMES — 'Treslin/TICRR', 'LAMP-2A/CMA', 'COPS5/JAB1' contain synonyms separated by '/'; treat each part as an independent alias and resolve whichever maps first.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What proteins interact with EGFR?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: general PPI query → ppi_association_string table only: association_gene_symbol (WHERE filter on EGFR), association_partner_gene_symbol (SELECT output), association_score (SELECT output for confidence context). annotation / protein_master columns are irrelevant — the user asked for partners, not function. physical and channel-score columns belong to separate tables and must be dropped.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What are EGFR's top interactors with experimental evidence?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: per-channel evidence query → ppi_detailed_channels_string table: channel_gene_symbol (WHERE filter on EGFR), channel_partner_gene_symbol (SELECT output), experimental (SELECT output — per-channel score, never a boolean filter), channel_combined_score (co-output required alongside any channel score). annotation and all association/physical columns from other tables must be dropped. Unused channel columns (neighborhood, fusion, cooccurence, coexpression, database, textmining) are also dropped.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What is the function of TP53 in STRING?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: annotation-only query → protein_master_table_string: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on TP53), annotation (SELECT output). ALL PPI edge columns from ppi_association, ppi_physical, and ppi_detailed_channels are completely irrelevant and must be dropped — the user asked for protein function, not interaction partners.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Does TP53 physically bind MDM2?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: physical binding check → ppi_physical_string table only: physical_gene_symbol (WHERE filter on TP53), physical_partner_gene_symbol (WHERE filter on MDM2 for a bidirectional existence check), physical_score (SELECT output for confidence). 'physically bind' / 'direct binding' / 'complex' keywords distinguish ppi_physical from ppi_association. annotation columns are irrelevant; channel-score columns belong to a different table.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Is K63-linked polyubiquitination used for proteasomal degradation?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: yes/no question about a ubiquitin chain-type mechanism → protein_master_table annotation: the rewriter expands 'K63-linked ubiquitin' to the key E2 enzymes [UBE2N, UBE2V1, UBE2V2]. Filter gene_symbol=[UBE2N, UBE2V1, UBE2V2], output annotation='requested'. The UBE2N annotation explicitly states whether K63 chains lead to proteasomal degradation. annotation is OUTPUT-ONLY — never add a filter value on it. NO PPI table needed.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What histone modifications do Polycomb repressor complex proteins deposit?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: list question about the enzymatic activities of a protein complex → protein_master_table annotation for each complex member: the rewriter expands 'Polycomb group / PRC2' to [EZH2, EED, SUZ12, RBBP4, JARID2]. Filter gene_symbol=[EZH2, EED, SUZ12, RBBP4, JARID2], output annotation='requested'. Each protein's annotation names the specific histone mark it deposits (H3K27me3 for EZH2, H2AK119Ub for RNF2, etc.). Do NOT use ppi_physical or ppi_association — the user asks what they DO, not who they interact with.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Does the PARP1-CTCF interaction exhibit circadian oscillation?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: yes/no PPI question with a non-PPI property STRING cannot answer (circadian oscillation, temporal) → ppi_association_string: filter association_gene_symbol=[PARP1], association_partner_gene_symbol=[CTCF], output association_score='requested'. The synthesizer will confirm the PPI edge exists with its score and explicitly state STRING has no temporal/circadian data. NEVER return zero results — the PPI component is answerable from STRING.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which are the main components of mTORC1?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: complex membership question → protein_master_table annotation for each known component: expand 'mTORC1' → gene_symbol IN [MTOR, RPTOR, MLST8, DEPTOR, AKT1S1], output annotation='requested'. Each subunit's annotation identifies its role in the complex. Do NOT query PPI tables — the user asks who is IN the complex, and the annotation directly names complex membership.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which proteins form the nuclear pore basket in human cells?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: complex membership question → protein_master_table annotation: expand 'nuclear pore basket' → gene_symbol IN [NUP153, NUP50, TPR, NUP98]. Output annotation='requested'. Each nucleoporin's annotation confirms basket localisation. Do NOT use PPI tables.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: List scaffold proteins of the ERK signaling pathway.
filter_few_shot_examples.note: list of functional protein class → protein_master_table annotation: expand 'ERK scaffold' → gene_symbol IN [KSR1, KSR2, IQGAP1, SHOC2]. Output annotation='requested'. Annotation confirms scaffold role for each. Do NOT use PPI tables.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Is there any link between CTF4 and CTF18 during sister chromatid cohesion?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: yes/no question using yeast gene names CTF4 and CTF18 → resolve via gene_alias_map: CTF4→WDHD1, CTF18→CHTF18. Query ppi_association_string: association_gene_symbol=[CHTF18], association_partner_gene_symbol=[WDHD1], output association_score='requested'. CHTF18-WDHD1 have association score 967. Synthesizer must recognise WDHD1 as the human ortholog of CTF4 and confirm the link.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Do U6-associated proteins Lsm4 and Lsm6 interact with SMN?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Three-entity functional interaction query (bare "interact" — no "physically") → ppi_association_string: association_gene_symbol (WHERE filter: [LSM4, LSM6]), association_partner_gene_symbol (WHERE filter: [SMN1]), association_score (output). NEVER select physical columns for bare "interact" — "physically" is required for ppi_physical.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Do the snRNA splicing proteins LSM1 and LSM3 physically interact in a complex?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Physical binding query ("physically interact") → ppi_physical_string: physical_gene_symbol (WHERE filter: [LSM1, LSM3]), physical_partner_gene_symbol (output), physical_score (output). Use ppi_physical ONLY when the user explicitly says "physically", "direct interaction", "co-complex", or "structural".

_comment: Schema rules for string. Injected into expander/filter/mapper prompts at runtime. GENERATED from dbs/string/schema.yaml by scripts/gen_schema.py — DO NOT EDIT.
db_description: STRING protein-protein association network — scored confidence interactions across seven evidence channels (physical binding, co-expression, text mining, curated databases, gene fusion, genomic neighbourhood, co-occurrence)

column_notes_override.association_gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol for the query side in ppi_association — p53→TP53
column_notes_override.association_score: INTEGER 700–999 in this snapshot (overall confidence across all channels). NOT a fraction.
column_notes_override.physical_gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol for the query side in ppi_physical — p53→TP53
column_notes_override.physical_score: INTEGER 700–999 in this snapshot (physical/binding evidence only). NOT a fraction.
column_notes_override.channel_gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol for the query side in ppi_detailed_channels — p53→TP53
column_notes_override.neighborhood: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). Set as 'requested' (output) when user asks about neighbourhood/genomic co-location scores.
column_notes_override.fusion: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). Set as 'requested' (output) when user asks about gene-fusion evidence.
column_notes_override.cooccurence: IMPORTANT: spelled 'cooccurence' (single 'r') on disk — use this exact spelling in all filters
column_notes_override.coexpression: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). Set as 'requested' (output) when user asks about co-expression evidence.
column_notes_override.experimental: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). When user asks for 'experimental evidence' or 'experimental score', set experimental='requested' (SELECT output), not a filter value. Only set it as a filter if the user specifies a numeric threshold (e.g. 'experimental > 500').
column_notes_override.database: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). Set as 'requested' (output) when user asks about curated-database evidence.
column_notes_override.textmining: INTEGER SCORE 0–1000 (NOT boolean). Set as 'requested' (output) when user asks about text-mining / literature evidence.
column_notes_override.channel_combined_score: INTEGER 700–999 in this snapshot (overall combined confidence). NOT a fraction.
